items.stem: A jewellery workshop makes necklaces and bracelets. Each unit of necklaces needs 2 hours on machine M₁ and 5 hours on machine M₂; each unit of bracelets needs 2 hours on M₁ and 3 hours on M₂. M₁ and M₂ are available for at most 31 and 20 hours a day. The profit is ₹50 per unit of necklaces and ₹35 per unit of bracelets. Formulate the linear programming problem to maximise profit.
items.answer: Maximise Z = 50x + 35y subject to 2x + 2y ≤ 31, 5x + 3y ≤ 20, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (x, y = units of necklaces, bracelets)
items.markingKey: Decision variables; objective function; constraints including non-negativity.

items.stem: A dietician wants a mixture of pulse mix and Food X. One kg of pulse mix contains 6 units of vitamin A and 4 units of vitamin C; one kg of Food X contains 5 units of vitamin A and 6 units of vitamin C. The mixture must contain at least 39 units of vitamin A and 19 units of vitamin C. pulse mix costs ₹20/kg and Food X costs ₹40/kg. Formulate the LPP to minimise cost.
items.answer: Minimise Z = 20x + 40y subject to 6x + 5y ≥ 39, 4x + 6y ≥ 19, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0
items.markingKey: Variables x, y = kg of each food (1 mark); objective (1 mark); constraints (1 mark).

items.stem: A sports goods factory in Indore makes cricket bats (x units) and hockey sticks (y units) per week. Each cricket bat takes 3 hours of labour and each hockey stick takes 5 hours; at most 33 labour hours are available. The store can hold at most 16 units in all. Profits are ₹20 and ₹35 per unit. (i) Write the objective function. (ii) Write all the constraints. (iii) Is (x, y) = (1, 1) a feasible point? Justify.
items.answer: (i) Maximise Z = 20x + 35y (ii) 3x + 5y ≤ 33, x + y ≤ 16, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (iii) Yes: 8 ≤ 33 and 2 ≤ 16
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark (ii) 2 marks (iii) 1 mark.

items.stem: A bakery makes cakes of kind P and cakes of kind Q. Each unit of cakes of kind P needs 3 hours on machine M₁ and 4 hours on machine M₂; each unit of cakes of kind Q needs 6 hours on M₁ and 3 hours on M₂. M₁ and M₂ are available for at most 42 and 27 hours a day. The profit is ₹40 per unit of cakes of kind P and ₹35 per unit of cakes of kind Q. Formulate the linear programming problem to maximise profit.
items.answer: Maximise Z = 40x + 35y subject to 3x + 6y ≤ 42, 4x + 3y ≤ 27, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (x, y = units of cakes of kind P, cakes of kind Q)

items.stem: Explain the difference between a feasible solution and an optimal solution of an LPP.

items.stem: A dietician wants a mixture of Food X and Food P. items.answer: (i) unbounded (ii) (0, 22), (8, 6), (14, 0) (iii) ₹98 at (14, 0); the half-plane 7x + 9y < 98 has no common point with the region

items.stem: Maximise Z = 8x + 8y subject to 4x + 4y ≤ 56, 5x + 4y ≤ 60, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0. Comment on the optimal solution.

items.stem: A furniture dealer makes tables and chairs. Each unit of tables needs 6 hours on machine M₁ and 5 hours on machine M₂; each unit of chairs needs 3 hours on M₁ and 5 hours on M₂. items.stem: A small factory in Bhopal makes screws A (x units) and screws B (y units) per week. items.answer: (i) Maximise Z = 30x + 35y (ii) 5x + 2y ≤ 53, x + y ≤ 14, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0 (iii) Yes: 7 ≤ 53 and 2 ≤ 14
